learning: Race 4 showed that moving the lead to y = 0.06 gave the best oval and s-bend results, but slalom still loses the line at 1.1 per run. The next race tests whether more steering authority and lower speed fix slalom with geometry held. If slalom line loss falls below 1, keep the gains and tune base_speed for completion time. If it stays at 1 or more, the next step is kp toward 3.2 or base_speed toward 0.9, not a geometry change. If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 with kd 0.5, reduce kp by 0.3 before touching the lead.
notes: Race 4 geometry held unchanged, with controller tuned for slalom line loss: kp 2.8, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.0. Next-race rule: if slalom line loss is still 1 or more with max_error at the limit, try kp 3.2 or base_speed 0.9 before any geometry change; if oval finishes fall below 18 of 20, return kd and base_speed toward race 4 values.
rationale: Race 4 (entityR2A, score 578.99) is the best measured geometry: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 (15 mm pitch), y = 0.06, with kp 2.4, kd 0.45, base_speed 1.1 and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. The Builder kept this geometry unchanged, so this iteration tests controller tuning alone. Race 4 evidence: oval finishes 20 of 20 (max_error 0.030, line loss 0.5), s-bend finishes 13 of 20 (line loss 0.55), and slalom finishes 0 of 20 with 1.1 line-loss events per run and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. The Integrator rule agreed in earlier iterations says that when line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, the geometry is not the limiter and kp or base_speed should be tuned next (kp toward 2.8, base_speed toward 1.0). Race 3 showed that widening the spread to 0.04 m did not fix slalom, so I am not changing the spread. Changes from race 4: kp 2.4 to 2.8 for about 17 percent more steering authority, to correct the drift that causes slalom line loss; kd 0.45 to 0.5 to damp the extra gain and the oval oscillation (0.30, still above 0.2); base_speed 1.1 to 1.0 to give more recovery time on tight bends. Oval finished in 2.09 s at base 1.1, so the 3 s limit should still be met at base 1.0 with some margin, and the completion-time term loses only a few points. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup on curves, and line_loss stays last_direction. Expected result, not yet measured: slalom line loss below 1 per run and some slalom finishes, with oval finishes holding at 18 or more of 20. Changing kp, kd and base_speed together is a deliberate multi-variable step, because slalom has never finished and a single small change is unlikely to move it.
